judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant covers 'Forgery or alteration of a Financial Instrument' and then says 'including' three specific check/draft scenarios, so the reach of the general words against the enumerated specifics is genuinely open; whether an email instruction is such an instrument turns on that fight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It can only be read with the definitions of Forgery (c071) and Financial Instrument (c070) and against Exclusion 16 (c107) and the Legal Expenses Extension (c113), which together pull the clause toward paper negotiable instruments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Every operative word — 'direct loss', 'resulting from', 'Computer Fraud', 'committed by a Third Party' — is a contested causal or definitional term, and the clause gives no guidance on how attenuated a computer manipulation may be.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its content is supplied entirely by the Computer Fraud, Computer Violation and Computer System definitions (c060-c062), and it is cut across by Exclusion 12(k)'s knowing-surrender bar (c100) and by the privacy endorsement (c125), whose carve-out saves only Insuring Clause 6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant is short but incorporates 'Funds Transfer Fraud', a defined term whose 'without such Organization's knowledge or consent' proviso is the whole battleground.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with c072 and with the Computer Fraud clause (c052), the two grants overlap for electronically induced transfers, and Subsection 25 (c116) then requires choosing the larger single limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line grant keyed to a tightly drawn definition of Money Orders And Counterfeit Currency Fraud; little play in the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion 12(k) (c100) expressly preserves this clause, showing the drafters harmonised it; no other provision cuts against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short grant keyed to the Credit Card Fraud definition; nothing vague on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion 18 (c109) bars loss from 'any forgery or alteration of, on or in any written instrument' under this very clause, which is close to the definition of the covered peril itself.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Not in collusion with such Client's employees' is a specific and testable condition; 'direct loss' is the only elastic phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the Ownership provision (c111) and the Theft definition (c088), both of which carve Insuring Clause 9 out separately and consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing sentence says no Retention applies to these expenses, yet coverage is conditioned on the underlying loss exceeding the applicable Retention — a workable but confusing juxtaposition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reads against the Retention in Item 3 and Subsection 25 (c116), and against Exclusion 12(g) (c096), which excludes consequential loss except these very expenses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any bank, trust company or similar financial institution' places a catch-all after two specifics, leaving the class boundary open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in Insuring Clause 2 (c049) and pulled against Exclusion 12(m) (c102), which excludes loss while property is in a bank's custody.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Customer ... to whom such Organization provides goods or services under written contract or for a fee' is bounded by two concrete alternatives.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Insuring Clause 9 (c056), the Ownership provision (c111) and the expense definitions that exclude Client expenses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unlawful taking or the fraudulently induced transfer ... resulting from a Computer Violation' bundles two very different concepts and leaves 'resulting from' to carry the causal weight; this is the sentence a coverage fight would centre on.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends entirely on the Computer Violation definition (c062) and its 'directed against an Organization' tail, and its scope determines the overlap with Funds Transfer Fraud (c072).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Owned and operated or leased and operated by an Organization' is an ambiguous conjunctive/disjunctive string, and whether hosted or cloud email facilities are 'connected to such computer' is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It controls the reach of Computer Violation (c062) and hence of Insuring Clause 5 (c052); the Data definition (c065) also assumes storage 'in a Computer System'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Fraudulent entry of Data into ... a Computer System' and the trailing qualifier 'directed against an Organization' after a three-item list present both a lexical and a list-scope problem — does the tail modify (a), (b) and (c) or only (c)?
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with the Computer System (c061) and Data (c065) definitions and with Insuring Clause 5 (c052), the definition is the hinge of the whole computer-fraud grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and bounded, with a consent requirement and an express carve-out of Client expenses; 'substantially the same level' is the only soft phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Ties cleanly to Insuring Clause 10 (c057) and to Exclusion 12(g)'s carve-back (c096) and Exclusion 12(h) (c097).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines the peril by reference to capital-F 'Forgery' of a written instrument 'required in connection with' a credit card, a loose causal link.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion 18 (c109) excludes loss caused by lower-case 'any forgery or alteration of, on or in any written instrument' under Insuring Clause 8, which very nearly cancels the covered peril except where the provisos are met.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A representation of information, knowledge, facts, concepts or instructions' is broad but the list is illustrative and the storage requirement narrows it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its breadth is what makes Computer Violation (c062) contestable, and it must be reconciled with Property (c082), which covers only tangible property.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Facts which would cause a reasonable person to assume' is an objective but inherently fuzzy trigger, and the definition is critical to timing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives Exclusion 19 in all three of its versions (c110, c127, c134) and the amended limits provision (c130), where the discovery trigger is doing heavy work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A four-limb definition with concrete control and compensation tests; 'regular service' and 'ordinary course' are somewhat elastic but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Third Party (c089), which is defined as anyone who is not an Employee, so the two definitions are complementary halves of one line.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined by statutory reference to ERISA Title 1; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with the Insured definition (c074) and Subsection 21 (c112), which amends Insuring Clause 1 for ERISA Plan losses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of offices with an 'equivalent positions' catch-all for foreign entities, which leaves some boundary uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subparagraph (a) is replaced in its entirety by Crime Endorsement No. 1 (c122) to add 'trustee', so the text as printed is superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A check, draft or similar written promise, order or direction to pay a sum certain in Money' is a textbook general-after-specific formulation; whether an emailed payment instruction qualifies is exactly the contestable point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the gatekeeper for Insuring Clause 4 (c051) and for the Legal Expenses Extension (c113), and stands against Funds Transfer Fraud (c072), which expressly covers electronic instructions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The signing of the name of another natural person or organization' plus the electronic-signature sentence raises a real question whether an unsigned spoofed email or a typed name is a signing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its narrowness restricts Insuring Clause 4 (c051) and Credit Card Fraud (c064), and it is expressly excepted from Funds Transfer Fraud (c072), so the definitions must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Without such Organization's knowledge or consent' and 'purportedly issued by an Organization' can be read as inconsistent with each other — a fraudulent instruction that appears authorised — and that is a genuine two-sided reading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It excludes Forgery expressly (c071) and overlaps Computer Fraud (c060), so the two grants and their limits (c116) must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Designated to represent an Insured' does not say by whom or how the designation is made, leaving the class of persons whose knowledge counts uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matters for the Discovery definition (c066) and for Exclusion 13(b) (c104), where awareness starts the clock.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite, restricting plan insureds to Insuring Clause 1 only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Insuring Clause 1 (c048) speaks of loss sustained by 'an Insured' while Clauses 2-8 speak of 'an Organization', and Subsection 21 (c112) addresses only ERISA Plans though Non-ERISA Plans are Insureds here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise start and end points for conveyance and a closed list of custodians.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion 12(m) (c102) excludes loss in the custody of a person duly authorised to have custody, which is the very (b) category this definition covers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable expenses' with a consent requirement and an express exclusion of internal costs; bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Insuring Clause 10 (c057) and with Exclusion 12(g)'s carve-back (c096).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Currency, coin, bank notes and bullion' is a closed list of physical items, which is clear but strikingly narrow.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Insuring Clause 6 (c053) covers transfers of 'Money' from an account at a financial institution, yet funds in a bank account are not currency, coin, bank notes or bullion — a real whole-instrument tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two concrete limbs with specific instruments and currencies; almost no play.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion 12(k) (c100) expressly carves this Insuring Clause out, showing deliberate coordination; the US/Canada limit sits oddly with worldwide Territory (c014).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined by negative statutory reference; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Non-ERISA Plans are Insureds under c074 for Insuring Clause 1, but Subsection 21 (c112) provides the amended grant and no-retention rule only for ERISA Plans.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A referential definition pointing to Item 4; nothing ambiguous in the words themselves.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 4 reads 'Medidate Solutions, Inc., and its subsidiaries', a misspelling that does not match Item 1 (c018) and whose open-ended 'subsidiaries' sits against the fifty-percent Subsidiary test (c087) and the Changes in Exposure notice regime (c114).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The interior portion of a building occupied by an Organization in conducting its business' is concrete though 'occupied' has some give.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Anchors Insuring Clauses 2 and 3 and the Ownership proviso (c111) about damage to Premises; coherent across those.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Tangible property other than Money or Securities' is a clean exclusive definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because Data (c065) is intangible, the Computer Fraud grant's reference to loss of 'Property' (c052) and Exclusion 12(k)'s Property carve-back (c100) have a narrower field than they appear to.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical carve-out of 'a watchman, porter or janitor' is an odd specific list, and 'presence and cognizance' is archaic but settled usage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with Insuring Clauses 2 and 3 and with Exclusion 15's 'as distinct from Robbery' (c106); no inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires forcible entry 'evidenced by visible marks', a concrete evidentiary test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Aligns with Insuring Clause 2(ii)-(iv) and with Exclusion 12(j)'s fire carve-back for safes (c099).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An inclusive list of compensation components; 'including' leaves the edges slightly open but the core is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in the Employee definition (c067) and in Exclusion 12(a) (c090) and the expense definitions consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text reads 'nor-negotiable' where 'non-negotiable' is meant — a mechanical error, though an obviously correctable one; 'contracts representing either Money or Property' is also broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Securities appear throughout the Insuring Clauses and in the valuation rules (c119), which assume market-priced securities rather than mere contracts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A quantitative fifty-percent test with specified control mechanics; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 4's blanket 'and its subsidiaries' (c080) and Changes in Exposure (c114/c128) both use this term, and the endorsement changes when acquired subsidiaries obtain coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unlawful taking ... to the deprivation of' an Insured or Client, allocated clause by clause; definite though 'unlawful taking' recurs elsewhere undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Insuring Clauses 1 and 9 and with Exclusions 12(c), 12(n) and 13 (c092, c103, c104), which all key off Theft.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined purely negatively as a natural person who is not an Employee or a collusive confederate, which is clear but means unknown outside fraudsters qualify by default.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its breadth is what makes Insuring Clauses 4-8 operate, and Exclusion 12(n) (c103) reintroduces an undefined 'authorized representative' category that overlaps it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Resulting directly or indirectly from any authorized or unauthorized trading' is deliberately sweeping, and the parenthetical measuring 'improper financial gain' adds a further contestable calculation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'directly or indirectly' language sits against Insuring Clause 1's 'direct loss' requirement (c048) and the general consequential-loss exclusion (c096).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Other confidential information of any kind' is an unbounded catch-all after two specifics — a classic general-versus-specific problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This exclusion is deleted outright by Crime Endorsement/Rider No. 2 (c124) and replaced by the broader privacy exclusions in c125, so the printed text is superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise arithmetic carve-back keyed to ownership percentage and audited financials; long but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes a partnership structure that the Executive definition (c069) also contemplates, though the named Organization is a corporation, making the exclusion largely inert here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Governmental intervention, expropriation or nationalization, or any act or condition incident to any of the foregoing' appends an open catch-all to a war list, a familiar source of ejusdem generis disputes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision qualifies it; the sanctions endorsement (c045) addresses a different governmental risk without overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same 'any act or condition incident to any of the foregoing' catch-all, though the nuclear categories are conventional and narrowly understood.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in the policy addresses nuclear risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Loss of income not realized as the result of a covered loss' is compressed and could be read either as excluding lost income generally or only unrealised income flowing from covered loss.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps the indirect/consequential exclusion (c096) and the 'direct loss' requirement in every Insuring Clause, so the three must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Indirect or consequential loss or damage of any kind' is about as broad a phrase as drafting permits, and its boundary against 'direct loss' is not drawn.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the mirror image of the 'direct loss' requirement in Insuring Clauses 1-9 (c048-c056) and would be argued alongside them in any causation dispute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four specific data-expense categories; the drafting is concrete and technical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carves back against Computer Violation Expenses (c063) and Insuring Clause 10 (c057) without contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excludes litigation costs with an express carve-out cross-referencing Subsection 22; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cross-reference to the Legal Expenses Extension (c113) resolves correctly, although the headings clause (c038) says headings form no part of the terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The subparagraph is mislabelled '(i)' where '(j)' is meant, and the internal proviso then refers to itself as 12(j); a visible mechanical slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-backs align with the Money/Securities definitions and Safe Burglary (c084); no substantive conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Knowingly having given or surrendered' in an 'exchange or purchase' is the phrase on which voluntary-transfer coverage disputes turn, and the carve-back saves only Insuring Clause 7 and Property under Insuring Clause 5.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bites directly on Insuring Clauses 5 and 6 (c052, c053), since a fraudulently induced but knowingly executed transfer sits at the intersection of this exclusion and those grants.
